newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Rugby Union - All Blacks return for North Harbour.
newsitem.headline: Rugby Union - All Blacks return for North Harbour.

text.p: AUCKLAND, Sept 6 - North Harbour are expecting nothing less than a torrid, no-frills battle when they host Wellington in their NPC first division rugby clash at Takapuna on Saturday, NZPA reports.

North Harbour go into the match with two losses from their first two matches and Meurant has been at pains this week to ease his players' minds after their narrow Ranfurly Shield loss to Taranaki last weekend.
"That is done with, we don't want to dwell on it. I'm bloody glad it is not an issue for us this week because we need to get championship points," Meurant said.
"We have to get full points this week and the team know how important it is that we step up our performance to another level."
Meurant has quickly recalled his All Blacks, apart from lock Ian Jones who was injured in South Africa but could return against Waikato for what could be a shield match next Friday night in Hamilton.
"The All Blacks have settled in really well. It's great to have them all back. You always miss the established combinations when they aren't there."
The major change to the North Harbour lineup is in the backs where Warren Burton returns to his more accustomed first five-eighth role.

The All Blacks midfield pairing of Walter Little and Frank Bunce will shore up the midfield, and in the three-quarters Harbour have the full power of the New Zealand sevens team with Glen Osborne at fullback and Peter Woods and Eric Rush on the wings.
Interestingly, promising Mark Robinson retains the halfback job ahead of Boyd Gillespie while Meurant has made only one change in the forwards.
Big Mark Weedon, expected to play a prominent role while the All Blacks were away, has paid the price for poor form in Harbour's first two games.
"Darren George has been giving it everything and that is due reward.
"We don't feel Mark's been in quite the form we saw of him last year and we expect him to improve," Meurant said.
All Black utility forward Blair Larsen returns to lock in place of Weedon and will jump at No 2 in the lineouts.

"We know Wellington have a big pack, they seem a more robust side than they were last year. I was very impressed with the way they went on to win with only 14 players on the field (against Canterbury last weekend)," Meurant said.
"There's no doubt about it, this is going to be extremely hard work for us, but I'm sure our team is up to scratch.
"The feeling in the squad has been good this week and I really feel our forwards are starting to make headway now."
Teams --

North Harbour: Glen Osborne, Eric Rush, Frank Bunce, Peter Woods, Walter Little, Warren Burton, Mark Robinson, Richard Turner (captain), Liam Barry, Darren George, Blair Larsen, Pat Lam, Gavin Walsh, Slade McFarland, Scott Palmer.
Reserves: Boyd Gillespie, Adam Larkin, Joe Mafileo, Mana Otai, Hayden Ferris, Mark Weedon, Steve Smith.

Wellington: Tana Umaga, Steve Skinnon, Alama Ieremia, Alex Telea, Jason O'Halloran (captain), Jon Preston, Joe Filemu, Isaac Feaunati, Gordon Simpson or Martin Leslie, Mike Russell, John Daniell, Inoke Afeaki, John Tanner, Tala Leiasamaivao, Mike Edwards.
